title: Transformational and Inclusive Leadership Communication in Driving Public Sector Organizational Change in the Digital Transformation Era
summary: This research examines the role of transformational leadership communication mechanisms in driving public sector organizational change in the digital transformation era, with a case study at the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia thru the "Kemenkeu Satu" application. A qualitative approach with a single case study design was used, focusing on the analysis of publicly documented leadership communication practices. Data was collected from secondary documents, such as leadership speeches and statements, news releases, official press releases, and public policy documents containing narratives of organizational integration, work values, and digital transformation agendas. Data analysis was conducted using thematic coding techniques to identify communication patterns that reflect the dimensions of transformational leadership and the strengthening of an inclusive climate. The research findings indicate that leadership communication serves as a managerial mechanism that unifies the direction of change, strengthens the legitimacy of the transformation, and manages the organization's internal diversity. The "Kemenkeu Satu" program is positioned as an integrative narrative that connects the vision of change, the value of integrity, cross-unit collaboration, and the drive for digital-based learning and innovation. This finding confirms that the success of public organizational transformation is not solely determined by formal policies and structures, but also by the consistency and quality of leadership communication in building shared meaning and workplace cultural cohesion. Practically, this research shows that change management in public organizations requires a consistent, inclusive, and continuous learning-oriented leadership communication strategy for digital transformation to be effective. This research enriches the public sector change management literature with thematic evidence on how leadership communication manages internal diversity to strengthen cultural cohesion and commitment to change. However, this study has some limitations, including reliance on secondary data which may limit direct understanding of individual contexts within the organization and potential interpretive bias from available documents.

title: Criminal Liability for the Manipulation of Financial Statements from the Perspective of Government Regulation Number 43 of 2025 Concerning Financial Reporting
summary: This study, entitled "Corporate Criminal Liability for Financial Statement Manipulation from the Perspective of Government Regulation Number 43 of 2025 concerning Financial Reporting," examines corporate financial statement manipulation (case studies of PT Garuda Indonesia Tbk and PT Hanson International Tbk) alongside the implications of Government Regulation (PP) No. 43 of 2025. It aims to analyze the imposition of sanctions on corporations engaging in financial statement manipulation and examine the role of PP No. 43 of 2025 as a mitigation tool for financial reporting crimes. Using a normative legal method with a descriptive-analytical specification, secondary data were collected through library research and analyzed normatively-qualitatively. The results show that corporate criminal liability is applied when intentionality (mens rea) in presenting false and misleading information is proven, rather than mere technical accounting errors. PP No. 43 of 2025 functions as a preventive and evidential mitigation instrument through reporting standardization, preparer competency requirements, mandatory liability statements, and the integration of the Joint Financial Reporting Platform (PBPK), which strengthens the chain of accountability and digital evidence for criminal law enforcement.

title: Neurosymbolic code auditing
summary: Code auditing examines whether an implementation satisfies target properties such as reliability, security, performance, and design intent. Classical static analysis provides rigorous foundations for automated auditing, but it remains difficult to apply broadly in real-world software. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) and agents creates new opportunities for leveraging semantic cues that are embedded in source code, documentation, and other software artifacts yet difficult for classical static analyzers to derive. This survey presents a comprehensive study of neurosymbolic code auditing, an emerging synthesis that integrates LLM-driven reasoning with classical static analysis and other structured program reasoning techniques. By formalizing the cognitive processes underlying manual code auditing, this study conceptualizes an agent-centric framework that serves as a unifying foundation for neurosymbolic analysis. Specifically, this study categorizes LLM-enabled primitive analyses over both code and non-code artifacts, addressing the fundamental reasoning tasks routinely performed by human auditors. Furthermore, the authors review a broad spectrum of neurosymbolic architectures that combine symbolic tools with LLM-based reasoning, illustrating how these systems replicate and extend the practical strategies employed by human auditors. Lastly, the authors synthesize the survey around three recurring bottlenecks, namely, observation, verification and memory, then outline future directions and the persistent technical challenges.

title: Climate change exposure and firm value in China: evidence consistent with a discount-rate interpretation
summary: This paper examines the relationship between firm-level climate change exposure and firm value in China. Using A-share listed firms from 2002 to 2020 and a disclosure-based measure of perceived climate change exposure, we find a significant negative association between climate change exposure and firm value. Our measure provides incremental explanatory power beyond conventional proxies, including ESG indicators and climate change news risk measures. Channel tests provide evidence consistent with a discount-rate interpretation. Both transition and physical-risk exposures are negatively associated with firm value. However, for firms in carbon-neutral industries, transition exposure is positively associated with firm value, consistent with transition-related growth opportunities. The negative associations are more pronounced for firms in high-pollution industries and coastal regions. Further results indicate that the negative valuation association is weaker among firms with stronger green innovation and ESG ratings. Overall, our findings highlight the pricing of climate risk and the role of transition opportunities in firm valuation.

title: A Review of the Impact of ESG Performance on Investment Portfolio Performance
summary: The relationship between ESG performance and investment portfolio performance has become a focal point of academic debate. This review systematically examines studies from 2009 to 2024 indexed in Web of Science, Scopus, and CNKI databases, organizing them around three interrelated questions: does ESG integration help or hurt returns, by what mechanisms does it operate, and why do empirical findings differ so sharply across studies? Three broad positions emerge. The positive school argues that ESG leadership builds intangible capital—stakeholder trust, and reputational resilience—that conventional financial metrics tend to miss. The negative school contends that ESG constraints narrow the investment universe and suppress expected returns. A third, more skeptical position holds that the divergence in findings is largely an artifact of inconsistent rating methodologies and sample choices rather than evidence for or against ESG per se. Empirical data from MSCI indices over 2016–2025 show ESG-screened portfolios performing on par with conventional benchmarks, with compound annual growth rates of 12.17% for both. The review finds that ESG integration is most reliably associated with reduced tail-risk exposure and lower financing costs, rather than with systematic outperformance. Whether it improves risk-adjusted returns depends heavily on which rating agency's scores are used, the market in question, and how the portfolio is constructed.

title: The Green Investment Paradox in Japan: Growth, Energy, and Financial Realities
summary: This study examines the concept of "green finance," a cornerstone of sustainable development, in the context of the Japanese economy, exploring its empirical and theoretical dimensions. The relationship between renewable energy consumption (RENE), GDP per capita, and foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows was econometrically tested using data from Japan for the period 1990-2024. ADF unit root tests applied within the econometric analysis framework showed that the variables were not stationary at their level values but became stationary (I(1)) after taking their first differences. The results of the "Bootstrap ARDL Bound Test" applied subsequently confirmed the existence of a long-term cointegration relationship between the variables. Japan has announced its Green Growth Strategy in line with its goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2050, and has become the second-largest green bond issuer in Asia. However, the analysis reveals that there are still significant gaps between goals and practices. Specifically, the increasing dependence on fossil fuels after nuclear energy, the slowness in investment and implementation processes, and the risks of "greenwashing" in ESG investments have been identified as the main challenges. title: Grid-based environmental governance and the energy transition of rural households: evidence from the China labor-force dynamics survey
summary: Introduction We examine whether grid-based environmental governance promotes clean cooking fuel use among rural households through local grassroots governance and public service delivery. Methods We exploit the staggered rollout across Chinese cities as a natural experiment and link policy timing to rural household panel data from the China Labor-force Dynamics Survey covering 2012 to 2018. A multi-period difference-in-differences design identifies the policy effect. Results The policy significantly increases clean cooking fuel adoption. The mechanism estimates suggest three main channels: wider social security coverage, greater participation in public affairs, and higher household income. Effects are stronger in areas with weaker digital infrastructure, higher levels of human capital or urbanization, and among households with younger heads. Discussion Embedding environmental duties in local information collection, case referral, and public service networks allows the policy to ease information and service constraints during rural household energy transition. The findings suggest that stronger grassroots environmental governance can promote clean energy use across rural areas.

title: Digital Transformation as an Organisational Change Process in Higher Education: A Qualitative Research at a Large Public University in Poland
summary: Digital transformation in higher education requires not only technology adoption but also effective organisational change management. While existing research has examined institutional strategies and technological infrastructure, limited attention has been paid to how system users perceive digitalisation during early implementation stages – a critical phase when resistance and uncertainty are most likely to emerge. This study addresses that gap by exploring user perceptions of digital transformation through the lens of change management theory. The research was conducted at a large public university in Poland undergoing digitalisation of administrative processes. An exploratory qualitative approach was adopted, involving four semi-structured interviews with administrative system users. The findings indicate that digital systems are generally perceived as beneficial for operational efficiency, but they also reveal challenges related to insufficient communication, unclear procedures, and inadequate preparation for change. These early-stage results highlight the importance of human-centered change strategies while ensuring alignment between technological implementation, organisational practices, and user competencies.

title: PROPERTY MANAGEMENT IN DEVELOPING NATIONS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF INSTITUTIONAL GAPS, DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION PATHWAYS, AND SUSTAINABILITY INTEGRATION
summary: Property management in developing nations remains constrained by fragmented institutional architecture, weak land administration systems, and the slow diffusion of digital and sustainability innovations. This study reviewed the synthesized evidence from 30 peer-reviewed studies, refereed conference proceedings, and foundational institutional-economics texts spanning Sub-Saharan Africa, South-East Asia, and comparable developing-economy contexts to examine three interlocking dimensions of the property management deficit: institutional gaps, digital transformation pathways, and sustainability integration. Anchored in New Institutional Economics and institutional-void theory, the review employs a structured literature-matrix methodology to map study context, method, and findings across the reviewed corpus. Findings indicate that institutional voids, manifest as regulatory fragmentation, weak enforcement, and professional informality, remain the primary constraint on effective property management, while digital tools such as blockchain-based land registries and property-technology platforms offer partial but institutionally contingent remedies. Sustainability integration, though increasingly prioritised globally, is impeded by financing, awareness, and regulatory barriers specific to developing-economy built environments. The review proposed an integrated institutional-digital-sustainability framework linking these three pillars and argues that digital transformation and sustainability initiatives can achieve durable impact only when embedded within institutional-strengthening interventions. The paper contributed a consolidated evidence base and framework for scholars, professional bodies, and policymakers engaged in property management reform in developing nations, while identifying methodological and geographic gaps warranting further empirical inquiry.

summary: This is an accepted article with a DOI pre-assigned that is not yet published.This study investigates the “double bind” faced by female leaders in Indonesia’s healthcare sector—an emerging market characterized by high masculinity, patriarchal norms, and a two-tier system. We examine how female commissioners and female directors influence firm performance and whether corporate governance mechanisms (such as audit committees, institutional ownership, and managerial ownership) mitigate the performance effects of gender incongruity. We used a sequential method, starting with archival research and then a focus group discussion. Using a panel of 214 firm-year observations from all listed healthcare companies on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2015–2024), we apply random-effects regression models to test direct and moderated relationships. The findings indicate that female commissioners and female directors are associated with significantly lower ROA, but this effect is attenuated by audit committees and institutional ownership. Our study thus extends the archival research results by identifying the factors that explain the process of female leadership.

title: Heterogeneous firm responses to a soft greenhouse gas disclosure regime: evidence from Hong Kong
summary: Purpose This study examines how firms respond to Hong Kong's 2017 greenhouse gas (GHG) disclosure requirement, a soft disclosure regime implemented on a comply-or-explain basis. The paper focuses on whether post-rule patterns differ between firms that voluntarily disclosed GHG emissions before the requirement and firms that disclosed GHG information for the first time after its introduction. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a sample of Stock Exchange of Hong Kong-listed firms subject to the 2017 GHG disclosure requirement and distinguishes between prior voluntary disclosers and first-time disclosers. Using a difference-in-differences design combined with propensity score matching, the paper examines three outcome domains: GHG emissions, selected operating and financial outcomes and reporting-related measures based on accrual-based and real-activity-based earnings management proxies. Additional analyses assess covariate balance, sample attrition, imputation validity, placebo tests and alternative emissions specifications. Findings The emissions analysis provides limited exploratory evidence of immediate short-run reductions in reported GHG emissions for either prior voluntary disclosers or first-time disclosers. Because observed pre-rule emissions are unavailable for first-time disclosers and most comparison firms, the emissions results rely partly on model-based estimates and should be interpreted cautiously. First-time disclosers exhibit more pronounced post-rule changes than prior voluntary disclosers in selected operating and financial outcomes, although these results are tentative because identification diagnostics are not uniformly supportive. The clearest evidence of heterogeneity appears in selected real-activity-based reporting measures, particularly abnormal operating cash flows and abnormal gains on asset sales. These patterns are consistent with reporting-related responses to increased ESG visibility and compliance burden, although they may also reflect genuine operating adjustments rather than opportunistic manipulation. Originality/value The paper contributes to the environmental disclosure and accounting literature by providing evidence from Hong Kong's soft GHG disclosure regime, an underexamined Asia-Pacific setting. By distinguishing between prior voluntary disclosers and first-time disclosers, the study highlights the role of disclosure readiness in shaping firm responses to sustainability reporting regulation. The findings suggest that, under a soft disclosure regime, heterogeneous short-run responses may appear more clearly in reporting-related operating measures than in immediate emissions reductions.

title: Artificial intelligence, digital transformation and green human resource management in Sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic literature review
summary: Purpose This study aims to systematically review the existing scholarship on the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation in enabling green human resource management (GHRM) within Sub-Saharan African (SSA) organisations. Drawing on 58 peer-reviewed articles published between 2018 and 2025, the review addresses two research questions: how AI and digital transformation technologies function as enablers of GHRM in SSA contexts and what contextual factors constrain or moderate their adoption and effectiveness in the region. The study responds to a notable gap in the GHRM literature, which remains disproportionately anchored in the Global North, by foregrounding the distinctive institutional, infrastructural and socio-technical realities of SSA. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 protocol and the management-domain SLR framework of Tranfield. Thematic content analysis was applied to synthesise findings across the selected corpus. Studies were sourced from Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO Business Source Complete, ProQuest and Google Scholar and rigorously assessed against structured inclusion and exclusion criteria. Quality appraisal was conducted using an adapted mixed-methods appraisal tool, yielding a final corpus of 58 studies for thematic synthesis. Findings AI and digital technologies encompassing big data analytics, cloud computing, AI-driven platforms and mobile learning tools function as multidimensional GHRM enablers in SSA organisations, with the strongest evidence concentrated in green recruitment, mobile-delivered green training and AI-enabled performance monitoring. However, their transformative potential is substantially constrained by an interconnected nexus of digital infrastructure deficits, digital skills gaps and institutional voids that characterise much of the region. The review proposes a contextually extended AMO framework that incorporates digital infrastructure adequacy, organisational AI capability and institutional governance quality as threshold boundary conditions on AI-GHRM effectiveness. Originality/value This review makes an original contribution by providing the first systematic synthesis of AI-enabled GHRM scholarship specifically focused on SSA. It integrates decolonial AI theory into GHRM discourse, proposes a contextually grounded theoretical framework with empirically testable propositions and advances a future research agenda focused on longitudinal, comparative and participatory scholarly engagement with one of the world’s most rapidly urbanising and environmentally vulnerable regions.

title: Bioremediation as a Sustainable Solution for Plastic Pollution under ESG Framework
summary: Plastic pollution has emerged as a critical global environmental challenge, threatening marine biodiversity and human health through the generation of microplastics. Conventional waste management methods, such as landfilling and incineration, often entail high greenhouse gas emissions and land-use limitations.Consequently, sustainable alternatives are urgently needed. This paper investigates whether bioremediation-specifically the use of enzymes and microorganisms to degrade plastics-offers a viable solution within the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework. Through a comparative analysis of traditional waste treatments and bioremediation technologies, supplemented by case studies of recent scientific and industrial applications, this study evaluates the sustainability of biological approaches. The findings suggest that while bioremediation holds significant potential to mitigate plastic waste and support the circular economy by reducing environmental impact, it is constrained by technological limitations, slow degradation rates, and economic costs. Therefore, bioremediation should be viewed not as a panacea, but as a complementary measure to reduction and recycling strategies. Its future application is promising but requires careful integration within the ESG framework.

title: ESG Performance and Financial Metrics in the Greek Passenger Shipping Sector
summary: This study examines the relationship between ESG performance and financial stability in the Greek passenger shipping industry. Technical efficiency is assessed using an input‑oriented Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA ), while the financial determinants of ESG performance are examined through Pooled OLS, Fixed Effect, and Logit models. The results show that ESG performance is positively associated with technical efficiency and profitability, and negatively related to credit risk and financial leverage, while firm size also exerts a positive effect. Overall, the findings highlight the strategic relevance of ESG adoption for sustainable growth and provide a practical assessment framework for sectors lacking standardized ESG rating systems, contributing to enhanced transparency and competitiveness in the passenger shipping industry.

title: THE IMPACT OF THE STOCK MARKET ON THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL ECONOMY OF UZBEKISTAN
summary: The development of Uzbekistan's stock market and its impact on the sustainable development of the national economy are examined, with particular emphasis on the financial-sector reforms implemented since 2017. As part of the broader liberalization process, particular attention has been given to strengthening the capital market, centered on the Tashkent Stock Exchange, as a mechanism for mobilizing domestic and foreign investment, diversifying enterprise financing sources beyond the banking sector, and supporting long-term sustainable economic growth. A significant milestone in this process was the admission in May 2026 of the National Investment Fund of the Republic of Uzbekistan (UzNIF), established by the Government of Uzbekistan in 2024 and managed by Franklin Templeton, to trading on the London Stock Exchange through global depositary receipts, alongside the simultaneous listing of its ordinary shares on the Tashkent Stock Exchange. The offering raised USD 603.6 million at a valuation of approximately USD 1.95 billion. The relationship between key indicators of stock market development – market capitalization, trading volume, the number of listed companies, and foreign portfolio investment – and indicators of sustainable economic development, including GDP growth, gross fixed capital formation, and economic diversification aimed at reducing dependence on raw materials, is investigated. Time-series data for the period following the 2017 liberalization reforms are analyzed using descriptive statistical, correlation, and regression methods, complemented by a case-study assessment of the UzNIF IPO. The findings indicate that, although Uzbekistan's stock market remains at an early stage of development relative to regional markets, the UzNIF listing has created new opportunities for attracting global institutional capital. Based on the findings, scientific and practical recommendations are developed for further strengthening capital market institutions, improving corporate governance and disclosure standards, attracting long-term institutional investment, and enhancing the stock market's contribution to the sustainable development of the national economy.

title: Fueling sustained green innovation advantage in Chinese listed firms: how AI orientation works through knowledge recombination and knowledge diversity
summary: Purpose Green innovation is critical to long-term advantage, yet sustaining it across multiple dimensions remains difficult. Drawing on the knowledge-based view, attention-based view and dynamic capability theory, this study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) orientation (AIO) promotes sustained green innovation advantage (SGIA) through knowledge mechanisms and under what conditions. Design/methodology/approach Using an unbalanced panel of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2001 to 2023, the authors combine annual-report text, patent and financial data. The authors measure AIO through text mining and validate it with alternative specifications, including an AI-clean measure that removes AI-washing. SGIA is modeled as an intertemporal, multidimensional construct encompassing quantity, quality, efficiency and speed. Main, mediation and conditional indirect effects are estimated using firm fixed effects. Findings AIO significantly improves SGIA and all four dimensions. Knowledge recombination creation (KRC) and knowledge recombination reuse (KRR) mediate these effects, while knowledge diversity (KD) more robustly strengthens the indirect pathway via KRR than via KRC. Originality/value This study conceptualizes SGIA as a multidimensional, intertemporal construct, distinguishes substantive AIO from symbolic AI narratives through AIW and AI-clean measures and identifies KRC and KRR as key mechanisms and KD as a selective boundary condition linking AIO to SGIA.

Time-series data for the period following the 2017 liberalization reforms are analyzed using descriptive statistical, correlation, and regression methods, complemented by a case-study assessment of the UzNIF IPO. The findings indicate that, although Uzbekistan's stock market remains at an early stage of development relative to regional markets, the UzNIF listing has created new opportunities for attracting global institutional capital. Based on the findings, scientific and practical recommendations are developed for further strengthening capital market institutions, improving corporate governance and disclosure standards, attracting long-term institutional investment, and enhancing the stock market's contribution to the sustainable development of the national economy.

title: Management Accounting and Strategy
summary: Management accounting strategy is a relatively new phenomenon in accounting. Management accounting in support of strategy, explores how management accounting can support the strategic management process of analysis, formulation, implementation, evaluation, monitoring, and control (Hopper, 2000). A management accountant must be knowledgeable about the operations of the company in order to bring value to it. In addition to accounting techniques, management accountants have access to strategy models and frameworks in their toolbox. Equipped with these diverse tools, the management accountant can make a substantial contribution to the company's worth. The main goal of management accounting is to give managers the information they need to run the company. As part of this, the organization's operational, business, and strategic decision-making processes are supported (Hilton et al., 2011). Many conventional accounting methods are said to be too inwardly focused, mainly financial in nature, and more appropriate for assisting with operational than with strategic decision making. Beginning in the early 1980s, writers proposed that accountants should conduct market research and offer information about rivals and competitors (Hopper, 2000). Accounting methods that prioritised the strategic elements of the company were distinguished from the more conventional, tried-and-true methods by using the term "strategic management accounting." This led to studies on the adoption of strategic management accounting techniques; however, the term is still uncommon among practicing accountants, and the applicability of these techniques is questionable. Organisations now operate in a more complex, dynamic, and unpredictable business environment. There isn't a better moment for management accountants to reach their full potential in aiding and assisting with the organization's strategic initiatives. Supporting all tiers of management during the course of the strategic management process is the goal of management accounting as strategy support. In order to highlight the connection between management accounting and strategy in the use of accounting data to further a company's strategic objectives, I have tried to examine management accounting from a wide perspective. I'll also look at how management accounting aids in the creation of complete and accurate financial statements for internal use, the assessment of outside data on rivals and industry trends, the conversion of goals into budgets and targets, and the tracking and management of business performance.

title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Disclosure, Eco‐Innovation, and Corporate Financial Performance: Insights From Sub‐Saharan African Markets
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure has become a crucial tool for demonstrating corporate accountability and sustainable development. While extensively studied in developed economies, its dynamics in emerging markets, particularly Sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA), remain underexplored. Grounded in stakeholder, resource‐based view, and legitimacy theories, we investigate the direct effects of environmental, social, and governance disclosure—denoted as environmental disclosure (ED), social disclosure (SD), and governance disclosure (GD)—on corporate financial performance (CFP), and the mediating role of eco‐innovation (EI). Using a sample of 264 listed firms from the manufacturing and energy sectors across four SSA sub‐regions (2010–2025) comprising 4224 firm‐year observations, we employ a two‐step System Generalised Method of Moments estimator with robust endogeneity checks. Our findings reveal a dimension‐specific impact: ED and SD significantly enhance CFP, while GD exhibits a significant negative direct relationship. Crucially, EI acts as a powerful mediator, not only strengthening the positive effects of ED and SD but also transforming the negative direct effect of GD into a positive net financial benefit. Further analysis reveals a U‐shaped relationship for ED and SD, indicating threshold effects. This study provides novel evidence that in SSA's evolving markets, technological eco‐innovation is the critical catalyst that unlocks the financial value of sustainability commitments, challenging one‐size‐fits‐all ESG perceptions. We therefore recommend that policymakers and managers in SSA adopt integrated strategies that couple substantive ESG transparency with targeted investments in eco‐innovation to advance sustainable development and secure robust financial returns simultaneously.

title: Digital Skills Competency, AI Readiness, and Job Performance of Nigerian Accounting Professionals
summary: This study examines the predictive relationships between digital skills competency, comprising digital literacy proficiency (DLP) and AI adoption capability (AIC), and the job performance of Nigerian accounting professionals, measured through task efficiency (TE) and reporting accuracy and quality (RAQ). Data from 132 valid survey responses collected across corporate, audit, and financial sectors were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. The evaluation of the outer measurement model confirmed valid internal consistency reliability and convergent validity (AVE > 0.50). Structural model analysis revealed that both exogenous constructs exert direct, statistically significant positive effects on performance outcomes. Specifically, DLP exhibits strong predictive pathways to both TE (β = 0.42, p < 0.001) and RAQ (β = 0.38, p < 0.001), whereas AIC drives TE (β = 0.31, p < 0.001) and RAQ (β = 0.36, p < 0.001). Concurrent path estimation indicates that the model explains 52% of the variance in task efficiency (R² = 0.52) and 55% of the variance in reporting quality (R² = 0.55). Consequently, the study recommends that organizations and professional bodies prioritize continuous digital upskilling and strategic AI adoption interventions.

title: Nexus between ESG disclosures and asset pricing efficiency in BRICS markets
summary: This study investigates whether the Environment, Social, and Governance (ESG) factor serves as a priced risk factor in explaining the portfolio returns of asset pricing models across the BRICS markets. Utilizing a characteristic-based portfolio construction approach, the study integrates ESG into standard asset pricing models such as Fama–French Three and Five Factor models, along with augmented and substitution factors, evaluating model performance using Gibbons, Ross and Shanken (GRS) F-statistic, spanning tests, and Sharpe ratio comparison over the period from April 2015 to December 2024. The empirical findings reveal that the ESG factor provides significant incremental explanatory power across BRICS markets. The spanning test confirms that ESG returns are not fully spanned by the existing FF factors, and factor-loading and Sharpe-ratio evidence are consistent with ESG carrying a priced risk premium. The cross-country analysis reveals heterogeneous patterns in ESG pricing: low-ESG portfolios show significantly negative ESG loadings, while high-ESG portfolios show significantly positive loadings within each market, with the most pronounced loadings observed in Brazil and China. Further, the results indicate that the ESG factor augments the existing five-factor model across all markets and effectively substitutes for the investment factor in India and China. The study provides evidence that the pricing relevance of ESG in BRICS asset markets is market-dependent rather than universal, offering insight into where and how ESG integration meaningfully improves sustainable investing frameworks across these heterogeneous economies.

title: Dynamic analysis, and offset boosting control of a new multi-echelon chaotic supply chain model with a sinusoidal nonlinearity for SDG-oriented resilient logistics
summary: Abstract This paper proposes a new multi-echelon 4-D chaotic supply chain model (NME-4D-CSCM) incorporating a sinusoidal nonlinearity to better represent uncertainties in supply chain dynamics. The model extends the existing framework by introducing periodic fluctuations in the supply-side variables, which significantly enhances the system’s complexity. The dynamical behavior of the proposed NME-4D-CSCM is investigated using phase portraits, bifurcation diagrams, and Lyapunov exponent (LE) spectra. Numerical results confirm the presence of chaotic attractors with higher sensitivity to initial conditions compared to the existing model, as indicated by larger maximum LE values. Stability analysis of equilibrium points is performed using the Jacobian matrix and eigenvalue analysis, revealing the instability of all equilibrium states. Furthermore, amplitude control is achieved through a rescaling method, allowing regulation of oscillation magnitude without altering the system’s chaotic nature. In addition, an offset boosting control strategy is implemented to shift the attractor position without affecting the underlying dynamics. The proposed NME-4D-CSCM provides a more comprehensive framework for analyzing complex behaviors in supply chain systems and offers practical control approaches for managing chaotic fluctuations.

title: Short Food Supply Chains as Pathways Towards Carbon-Neutral Rural Development: A Logistics-Adjusted Scenario Analysis for Fresh Produce in Galicia, Spain
summary: Short food supply chains (SFSCs) are often assumed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions because food travels fewer kilometers. That inference is incomplete when vehicle size, payload, chain stages and empty returns differ between short and conventional distribution. This study develops a transparent, logistics-adjusted scenario model for one tonne of fresh, unprocessed, non-frozen horticultural produce delivered to a point of sale in Ferrolterra, Galicia. Four configurations are compared: a direct producer-to-market SFSC, coordinated regional SFSC, optimized conventional long chain and fragmented conventional long chain. Representative road corridors connect As Pontes with Ferrol (43.1 km) and Almería with Ferrol (1144.3 km), but the analysis is explicitly prospective rather than an observation of actual trade flows. Well-to-wheel emissions are calculated from 2025 official vehicle-kilometer factors, differentiated by vehicle class and load, and propagated through 100,000 Monte Carlo iterations. Median emissions were 63.4 kg CO2e t−1 for a direct SFSC, 22.0 for a coordinated SFSC, 113.5 for the optimized long chain and 184.0 for the fragmented long chain. Direct SFSC emissions were lower than the optimized benchmark in 95.8% of simulations, but its 95% interval for relative reduction included a small disadvantage (−7.7% to 67.9%). Load factor was the dominant driver of direct-SFSC uncertainty (Spearman ρ = −0.866). At the representative local distance, the van required a payload above approximately 0.263 t to outperform the median optimized long-chain scenario. The results show that proximity is neither necessary nor sufficient for lower transport emissions: coordination and consolidation determine whether distance advantages are realized. SFSCs may support rural transition strategies, but claims about whole-food-system carbon neutrality or rural-development outcomes require empirical logistics data and full life-cycle assessment.

title: DECISION-SUPPORT FRAMEWORK FOR MULTIDIMENSIONAL ESG PERFORMANCE EVALUATION IN THE BANKING SECTOR
summary: For financial institutions, sustainable development has become a priority concern for both the investors and the sector. This manuscript suggests a holistic decision-making approach for the sustainability evaluation of deposit banks by integrating the CRISUS, MSD, and AROMAN algorithms. Building on earlier research, this research uses a multi-criteria assessment framework encompassing three main dimensions (environmental, social, and governance) and 15 indicators within the scope of sustainability. Using this introduced model, the research conducts a holistic assessment of the ESG performance of eight Turkish commercial banks. The results reveal that environmental criteria – particularly total greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy usage rate, and green loan rate – have the strongest impact on ESG performance, and Garanti BBVA demonstrates the highest performance among the analyzed banks. In conclusion, the hybrid approach introduced in this manuscript provides a robust and reliable decision support tool for implementers and decision makers for analyzing and improving the sustainable development strategies in banking.

title: CEO Compensation and ESG Performance: The Influence of Financial Outcomes and CEO Power
summary: ABSTRACT This study reviews literature at the intersection of CEO compensation and ESG goals. Combining an integrated bibliometric and structured literature review with an empirical analysis of US publicly listed companies from 2013 to 2023, the paper identifies a central governance tension where ESG performance is increasingly considered in CEO compensation decisions while also creating potential room for managerial opportunism. The empirical analysis investigates whether ESG performance is reflected in CEO compensation and whether this relationship is moderated by financial performance and CEO power. The findings reveal a positive association between ESG performance and CEO compensation, with stronger effects when CEOs also hold board chair positions, suggesting that powerful CEOs may use ESG performance to justify higher compensation. Additional analyses show that environmental and social performance are more strongly associated with CEO compensation than governance performance, while the interaction between ESG performance and CEO duality becomes more pronounced in firms with weaker financial performance. The results further indicate that ESG performance remains a stable determinant of CEO compensation over time and becomes more salient following the institutionalisation of ESG practices after 2018. Overall, the findings connect the review and empirical evidence by suggesting that the relationship between ESG performance and CEO compensation is influenced by the concentration of managerial power. This study provides a deeper understanding of ESG performance and CEO compensation dynamics and calls for more transparent compensation structures that are more aligned with stakeholder expectations.

title: Evaluating the Determinants and Organizational Outcomes of Information Technology Adoption in Financial Reporting and Operations: Evidence from a Quantitative Study
summary: The integration of information technology (IT) into financial reporting has transformed the landscape of organisational operations, yet its adoption remains uneven across sectors, particularly in emerging economies. This study investigates the determinants and outcomes of IT adoption in financial reporting and operational efficiency using a quantitative approach involving 100 respondents from various financial and administrative units. The research focused on key variables including efficiency, data accuracy, cost, flexibility, and quality of financial information. Descriptive analysis revealed that accessibility of information and security were highly rated drivers of adoption, with mean scores of 4.06 and 3.92, respectively, while flexibility recorded a comparatively lower mean of 2.62, indicating a significant implementation challenge. Inferential analysis using regression showed that efficiency (β = .620, p < .001), faster data processing (β = .511, p < .001), and quality of financial reporting (β = .152, p < .001) were strong predictors of IT adoption, while profitability and functionality were statistically less influential. The findings align with existing theoretical constructs such as the Technology Acceptance Model, emphasising perceived usefulness as a critical motivator. Moreover, high maintenance and training costs emerged as major barriers, reflecting the need for strategic financial planning and institutional support. The study contributes to the growing body of literature by offering empirical insights tailored to developing contexts and proposes practical recommendations for policy, capacity-building, and system design. The implications extend to organisational leaders and policymakers aiming to foster innovation and accountability through IT-enhanced financial systems.

title: Exploring the nexus between expert systems and sustainable development goals in the Palestinian public sector: the mediating role of audit quality
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate the nexus between expert systems and the compliance level with sustainable development goals. Furthermore, it aims to explore the mediating influence of audit quality. Design/methodology/approach To empirically examine the study model, a descriptive analytical approach has been adopted and executed in a rigorous manner. The data were gathered using a survey. More plainly, 133 surveys were distributed to employees in the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy, State of Palestine. Partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was carried out to examine the proposed hypotheses. Findings The findings reveal that expert systems as a key artificial intelligence model, have a positive and statistically significant impact on sustainable development goals attainment. Notwithstanding, the outcomes unveil that audit quality exerts a positive, albeit insignificant, mediating impact. Theoretically, the study results endorse the argument that sustainable development goals are predominantly action-oriented and reinforced by organizational capabilities rather than being merely contingent on governance mechanisms. More specifically, in unstable contexts, expert systems enhance internal informational capabilities and mitigate dependence on conventional governance systems such as audit quality, consequently exerting a direct impact on compliance with sustainable development goals. Practical implications The outcomes highlight the significance of increasing investment in expert system models and strengthening institutional audit frameworks, particularly in unstable and resource-constrained contexts, to foster ongoing engagement in sustainable development goals practices. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first study that evaluates the impact of expert systems on sustainable development goals attainment by testing audit quality as a mediating factor. The analysis reveals a novel result indicating no mediating effect of audit quality, as expert systems reinforce internal informational capabilities and alleviate reliance on audit mechanisms, yielding a more direct influence on sustainability compliance.

title: Pengaruh Sustainability Reporting (Sr) Dan Good Corporate Governance (GCG) Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan Pada Pt Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk Periode 2015 – 2024
summary: This study aims to determine and obtain empirical evidence regarding the effect of Sustainability Reporting and Good Corporate Governance, proxied by Independent Commissioners, on Firm Value. Sustainability Reporting is measured using the Sustainability Report Disclosure Index (SRDI) based on the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) G4 indicators. Good Corporate Governance is proxied by the proportion of Independent Commissioners, which is measured by comparing the number of Independent Commissioners to the total number of members of the Board of Commissioners. Firm Value is measured using the Price to Book Value (PBV) ratio. The population of this study is PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk, which is listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2015–2024 period. The sampling technique used is saturated sampling, in which all data during the observation period are used as the research sample, resulting in 10 observations. This study employs secondary data using a quantitative research method. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression analysis with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics version 25. The results of this study indicate that Sustainability Reporting and Independent Commissioners simultaneously have no significant effect on Firm Value. Partially, Sustainability Reporting has no significant effect on Firm Value, and Independent Commissioners also have no significant effect on Firm Value.

title: Doğrudan Yabancı Yatırımlar, Yeşil İnovasyon ve Ekonomik Büyüme İlişkisi: OECD Ülkeleri Üzerine Panel Nedensellik Analizi
summary: The liberalization of trade among countries and the removal of trade barriers have not only increased the importance of foreign direct investment (FDI) but also accelerated its inflows. One of the key macroeconomic variables affected by FDI inflows is economic growth. Meanwhile, green innovation, which refers to environmentally friendly technologies, has emerged as a crucial component of sustainable development. In recent years, green innovation has gained increasing importance not only in developed countries but also in developing economies. This study aims to examine the causal relationship between economic growth, FDI, and green innovation for 34 OECD countries over the period 2002–2021. The Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel causality approach is employed for the analysis. The empirical findings indicate the existence of a unidirectional causality running from economic growth to both FDI and green innovation. These results suggest that economic growth serves as a key driving force for both FDI and green innovation in OECD countries. In this context, policies aimed at increasing FDI should be supported by strategies that promote sustainable growth. Furthermore, the unidirectional causality from economic growth to green innovation implies that green innovation, rather than being a direct driver of economic growth, emerges as an outcome of the growth process in these countries.

title: Strengthening Co-Determination in Digital Transformation: A Qualitative Approach to Enhancing Works Councils’ AI Literacy and Capability for Socio-Ethical Reflection
summary: Abstract The accelerating digital transformation, and particularly the diffusion of generative AI technologies, poses profound challenges for workplace co-determination. Works councils increasingly face the need to assess and negotiate technological innovations under conditions of epistemic asymmetry, time pressure, and limited experience in (socio)-technical reflection. This paper introduces the Implication Canvas, an adapted version of the Implication Fan developed at the Berlin Ethics Lab, as a participatory tool to strengthen deliberative capacity in co-determination contexts with a focus on socio-ethical reflection. Drawing on an explorative qualitative research design, including participatory observation and post-workshop surveys, the study examines iterative adaptations of the canvas in three workshops with a cooperating works council. Findings indicate that the adapted canvas facilitates structured reflection on preconditions, consequences, and solution pathways of AI-driven workplace innovations while bridging communicative and epistemic gaps between management, technical experts, and employee representatives. The study argues that effective and responsible co-determination should be understood as an integrative competence combining technical orientation, ethical reflexivity, and procedural agency. Participatory reflection tools such as the Implication Canvas can support the practical enactment of this competence and contribute to more inclusive and responsible workplace AI governance.

title: The dual role of transnational corporations in the implementation of Russia’s environmental policy: the experience of arctic projects
summary: The article examines the influence of large corporations with transnational status on the environmental situation in the Russian Arctic. The author proceeds from the fact that the role of these structures is ambiguous: they simultaneously act as both investors in environmental technologies and a factor in the preservation of outdated environmentally hazardous industries. The work uses systemic and institutional approaches, as well as content analysis of the reporting of key players – Norilsk Nickel, Gazprom Neft, and Severstal. It is shown that after 2022, the system of incentives for environmental modernization has radically changed. The loss of access to Western capital markets has reduced the importance of ESG criteria, but businesses have not abandoned environmental rhetoric. Instead, there has been a reorientation to domestic objectives – participation in national projects, work in the BRICS format, and the formation of a sovereign sustainable development agenda. The main conclusion is that the Arctic has become a testing ground where the conflict between economy and ecology is most acute, and therefore, an adjustment of state control mechanisms is required.

title: From Reactive Compliance to Predictive Resilience: Governed AI for Knowledge Management and Supply Chain Integration in Class II Medical Device Operations – A Case Study
summary: Small and mid-sized Class II medical device manufacturers face a scale-up challenge when regulatory, quality, and supply chain information grows faster than the organization’s ability to manage it. This paper examines whether governed artificial intelligence can convert fragmented records into decision-ready knowledge without weakening compliance, traceability, or human accountability. Using an applied case-study design, the research evaluates a six-month pilot at New Horizon Biotech, an anonymized Class II diabetes device manufacturer. A five-FTE AI Business Unit connected regulatory evidence, supplier records, quality documentation, and operational signals through a dual-loop model. The Regulatory Readiness Loop supported evidence retrieval, predicate comparison, submission drafting, and EU MDR GSPR mapping. The Supply Adaptation Loop supported supplier early warning, alternate-source readiness, change impact review, and landed-cost analysis. Pilot results showed a 32.3% reduction in drafting cycle time, 67.8% reduction in defect density, 88.0% reduction in evidence retrieval time, 38.8% faster lead-time recovery, zero critical stockouts, a Month 6 groundedness score of 0.94, and an 82.4% six-month ROI. The findings suggest that governed AI can support regulatory throughput and supply resilience when it is implemented as controlled knowledge infrastructure rather than autonomous decision-making.
